rows.grounds: first member of compound expressing the cause of accomplishment; satisfaction of the guru
indicates sufficiency of the preceding cause alone
describes a practitioner whose mantra is defective; compound qualifying the implied subject
emphasizes that success occurs despite the defect

items.question: Is the guru's satisfaction alone sufficient for accomplishment despite a defective mantra?
premises: Spiritual accomplishment can depend on the guru's satisfaction.
A practitioner may possess a faulty or defective mantra.
The mere satisfaction of the guru can outweigh defects in practice.
items.inference: Therefore, even a practitioner with a defective mantra attains success through the guru's satisfaction alone.
uncertainties: The internal compound structure of duṣṭa+mantraḥ may be read as karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi.
items.plain_english: Even one who has a faulty mantra succeeds through the mere satisfaction of the guru.
